blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: India is broadly divided into six major physiographic divisions: The Himalayan Mountains, Northern Plains, Peninsular Plateau, Indian Desert, Coastal Plains, and Islands.
The Himalayas are geologically young fold mountains stretching along India's northern border, divided longitudinally into Himadri, Himachal, and Shiwaliks.
The Peninsular Plateau is the oldest and most stable landmass in India, composed of igneous and metamorphic rocks formed from Gondwanaland.
The Northern Plains are rich alluvial deposits created by the Indus, Ganga, and Brahmaputra river systems.
The Western Ghats form a continuous elevated boundary on the west coast, whereas the Eastern Ghats are discontinuous and dissected by major east-flowing rivers.
